title: Lena and the Drop
premise: Dominic Eriksen, a fixer for the Meridian Group — an embassy that exists on no map and answers to no flag — discovers that a safe house he has used for two decades has been listed for sale online, its interior photographed down to the hidden documents. The listing is a message: someone inside the network that trained him is selling them out, one room at a time. With his handler dead and his protégé Lena Voss the only person he can still trust, Dominic must trace the leak through the very tradecraft they were taught, burning each node of the network before it burns them. In the end, Dominic sacrifices himself to destroy the Group's archive, and Lena — who was never supposed to survive her training — walks away carrying both the evidence and the choice to finally belong to no one but herself.
about_author: Coral Underhill is the pen name of a former logistics consultant who spent years drafting contingency plans for organizations she was never allowed to name. She writes thrillers about people whose loyalties are contractual rather than chosen.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Scrolling property listings in a Vienna café, he freezes on a familiar address: Safe House 7, listed with interior photos showing the wall safe open. He recognizes the staging as Meridian protocol. Emotional beat: cold dread beneath professional calm — twenty years of rules just became evidence.

chapters.title: Protocol for Ghosts
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena runs counter-surveillance to meet Dominic, noting how thoroughly she was trained to distrust even him. They compare notes: three other safe houses have appeared on listings across Europe. Emotional beat: wary intimacy between mentor and protégé, love neither will name.

chapters.title: Dead Handler
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Their handler, Marta, misses a scheduled contact; Dominic finds her flat sanitized to Meridian standards — too clean, days early. A single clue survives: a printed page of the listing with an estate agent's initials. Emotional beat: grief compressed into procedure; the rules offer no comfort.

chapters.title: The Estate Agent
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena poses as a buyer and meets the agent, who genuinely believes she works for a boutique firm called Halloway & Finch — a shell that dissolved six years ago. Someone resurrected a dead company to sell dead houses. Emotional beat: the uncanny thrill of touching the enemy's handiwork.

chapters.title: What We Were Taught
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, with flashbacks to the training facility at Kestrel Point. He realizes the listing photos are framed exactly like training slideshows — this is a lesson being taught, not a sale. Emotional beat: the horror of recognizing your own curriculum turned against you.

chapters.title: Halloway & Finch
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Digging into the shell company, Lena finds its registered director died in 2019 — yet signatures on recent filings are flawless forgeries of his hand. Only Kestrel Point graduates could forge like this. Emotional beat: belonging curdling into suspicion; the traitor is one of them.

chapters.title: Twelve Names
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. From memory, he reconstructs the roster of his graduating cohort — twelve names, four confirmed dead. Cross-referencing the listings' posting times against known locations narrows the field to three. Emotional beat: the loneliness of a man whose entire social world is a suspect pool.

chapters.title: Amsterdam Dead Drop
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena retrieves a cache from an old drop and finds it already emptied — replaced with a photograph of herself entering the canal house an hour earlier. Emotional beat: naked fear; she has been watched by someone fluent in her own habits.

chapters.title: The Buyer
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. An anonymous inquiry offers to buy 'the network, not the houses.' Dominic stalls the negotiation to trace routing, discovering the messages originate from inside Meridian's own communications relay. Emotional beat: vertigo — the rot isn't beside them, it's above them.

chapters.title: Rules Rewritten
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. New orders arrive through official channels: terminate Eriksen, preserve the archive. Lena must choose between the duty drilled into her and the man who taught her everything. Emotional beat: love against duty made literal; she burns the order unread by anyone else.

chapters.title: Kestrel Point
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. They infiltrate the decommissioned training facility, finding it recently reoccupied — classrooms restaged, the slideshow of safe-house photos looping on a projector. It's a rehearsal space for their deaths. Emotional beat: returning to the scene of your making as a stranger.

chapters.title: Cohort
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. In the facility's records, Lena identifies the survivor behind Halloway & Finch: Ilse Brandt, the instructor who designed the forgery module — presumed retired, actually running a private auction of Meridian's secrets. Emotional beat: fury braided with reluctant respect for a master at work.

chapters.title: The Auction
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Brandt's plan emerges: sell the network's full architecture to the highest bidder, using the listings as proof of authenticity. The sale closes in nine days. Emotional beat: the clock becomes a character; every hour of caution is a concession.

chapters.title: Safe House 7
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. They return to the original listed house to recover Marta's hidden ledger and walk into a staged viewing — real buyers, real agent, Brandt watching from the garden. Emotional beat: performing normalcy while dying inside; Lena holds a stranger's coffee and lies beautifully.

chapters.title: Marta's Ledger
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The ledger reveals Marta discovered the leak months ago and was feeding disinformation into the listings — meaning some of what they've traced is bait she laid. Emotional beat: posthumous loyalty from a woman who never said she cared; Dominic weeps once, briefly, then stops.

chapters.title: Bait and Switch
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Following Marta's disinformation trail backward, Lena locates Brandt's true archive vault beneath a Zurich private bank — but realizes Brandt expects them to find it. Emotional beat: the trap's elegance almost admires itself; Lena decides elegance can be weaponized.

chapters.title: Ilse Brandt
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic confronts Brandt at a gallery opening. She offers him partnership: the network deserves to outlive the institution that abandoned it. He refuses; she lets him leave, which frightens him more than a fight would. Emotional beat: two teachers measuring each other across a chasm of ideology.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Meridian activates every remaining asset against them. Lena executes a week of running contacts, spending caches, aliases, and friendships to keep Dominic moving. Emotional beat: survival priced item by item; each burned resource is a small funeral.

chapters.title: The Vault
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. They enter the Zurich vault during Brandt's own diversion — she's robbing Meridian's relay simultaneously. Dominic initiates the archive's thermite failsafe as Brandt's team breaches. Emotional beat: climax; Dominic stays with the burning archive so the destruction completes, buying Lena the exit.

chapters.title: What Survives
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena escapes with the one copy Brandt kept outside the vault — the complete Kestrel Point curriculum, including her own file marked 'do not survive placement.' Emotional beat: reading your own death warrant written years ago; grief and clarity arriving together.

chapters.title: Settlement
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena leaks the curriculum to journalists across four countries, dissolving Meridian's deniability forever, then visits Dominic's unmarked grave under a name he chose himself. Emotional beat: mourning without ceremony; the price of survival paid in full and counted honestly.

chapters.title: No Forwarding Address
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, final chapter. Months later, Lena spots a new property listing with a photo that contains a message only she could read — Dominic alive, off-grid, offering nothing but proof of life. She smiles, deletes it, and books a train to nowhere in particular. Emotional beat: belonging finally chosen, not assigned; an ending that is a beginning.
